messages.subject: Re: questions about nat package and DBM
messages.subject_clean: questions about nat package and DBM
messages.body_plain:
Dear Diego,

On 16 Sep 2017, at 0:49, Diego A. Pacheco Pinedo wrote:

> 1) I have recently been using your “nat” package, which is
> wonderful by the way!.

I am glad that it has proven useful. If and when you use nat in any work
submitted for publication, it would be great if you check in with me, if
there is a more current citation – continued work must be justified.

> I have a couple of questions regarding operations with a group of
> neuronlist (swc imported traces), I was wondering if there are
> functions to measure basic statistics of a collection of traces, for
> example:

> a) a function to measure the dispersion at a given orthogonal plane
> (relative to the traces)

This is something that I have done in analyses for papers e.g. Yu et al
2010 Cur Biol. The functions that I used are here:

   https://github.com/jefferis/AnalysisSuite/blob/master/R/Code/Geometry/Geometry.R

The code is a little old so it is not as polished, but you can use these
functions via the package nat.as <http://nat.as>

   https://github.com/jefferis/nat.as

Note that there is a (short but) slightly non-standard installation
procedure so read the README.

That said, I have actually started revising some of this old code to
meet the standards of newer, better documented and more robust code
already included in nat. You can see this work here:

   https://github.com/jefferis/nat/tree/feature/neurogeom

and install that development version of the package

   devtools::install_github("jefferis@feature/neurogeom")

In particular, there is a vignette, which provides a detailed walk
through of more or less what you want to do:

   https://github.com/jefferis/nat/blob/feature/neurogeom/vignettes/NeuroGeometry.Rmd

(you should be able to "knit" this in RStudio after installing the
neurogeom development branch as described above).

> b) a function to get an average trace from a collection of traces.

The catnat package from my student Alex Bates

   https://github.com/alexanderbates/catnat

includes a function average.tracts that will make an average of a set of
unbranched traces. You can turn a set of branched tracings into
unbranched tracings e.g. by making use of the spine function:

   http://jefferis.github.io/nat/reference/spine.html

which finds the longest path across the neuron, optionally starting from
the soma.

Making an average trace out of a set of branched tracings is
conceptually more difficult and there is not currently an
implementation. Your approach would depend partly on what you want to do
with the result. For example it may be easier to use the dotprops
version of the neurons but you would sacrifice the fully connected tree.

I remember that there is a plugin in Vaa3d consensus_skeleton that may
do what you want – however I cannot vouch for the output as I have
never tried it myself in earnest. The source code for the plugin is here
– this should ensure that you find the corresponding plugin in the
binary download of Vaa3D

   https://github.com/Vaa3D/vaa3d_tools/tree/master/released_plugins/v3d_plugins/consensus_skeleton

Best wishes,

Greg.

PS Please note that I have cced the nat-user google group in the hope
that some of these responses could be useful to others.

Best,

Greg.

--

messages.subject: Re: Ask about NBLAST
messages.body_plain:
Dear Xianyuan Zhang,

On 25 Sep 2017, at 3:32, Zhang Xianyuan wrote:

> I am Xianyuan Zhang, a PhD student from Dr. Adam Claridge-Chang Lab. I
> have 2 questions about using NBLAST.

Thanks for your interest and sorry for the slightly delayed response.

> I tried to use NBLAST online but it seems that the server is down. Can
> you help with it?

I'm afraid the server is running on a rather small machine and I think
it was overwhelmed by external requests during a training session in the
US. I have restarted the process and it is running again now.

The virtualflybrain.org <http://virtualflybrain.org> project has recently received a new 4y grant
from the Wellcome Trust and they will be purchasing a new machine with
much more memory to run this service going forwards, which will be much
more robust.

> The second question is if I want to use NBLAST locally, how can I get
> the full set of flycircuit neurons?

Yes, please see this thread:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/nat-user/PKkBAphpHcQ

for how to get the flycircuit dataset to run NBLAST locally.

Best wishes,

Greg Jefferis.

PS please note that I have cced the nat-user google group in case these
answers may be helpful for others in future.

messages.subject: Thoracic Ganglia
messages.body_plain:
Is it possible to use NBLAST on the neurons of the Thoracic Ganglia? If not, are there plans to add this brain region in the future?

Thank you,

Tyler Kennedy

messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Thoracic Ganglia
messages.body_plain:
Algorithmically yes. But we do not have any preprocessed data. In particular we do not have eg registered versions of GMR collection available. Best, Greg.

Sent from my iPhone
